concepts.title: What Percentage Really Means
concepts.simple: Percentage means 'out of 100'. 25% literally means 25 out of every 100. Before using formulas, convert the sentence into this idea.
concepts.visual:
100 boxes → 25 selected
25 / 100 = 25%
concepts.rule: Percentage = (Part ÷ Total) × 100

examples.question: 18% of a class is 9 students. Find class strength.

concepts.mistakes: Do not divide by the new value when percentage change asks for change from the original.

concepts.title: Percentage of a Number
concepts.simple: 'x% of y' always means x/100 × y. Simplify before multiplying.
concepts.visual:
x% of y
= x/100 × y
concepts.rule: x% of y = x×y/100
concepts.shortcut: Cancel 100 with the number first whenever possible.
concepts.mistakes: Do not multiply first if easy cancellation makes the calculation simpler.

concepts.title: Increase, Decrease and Successive Change
concepts.simple: Every percentage change is applied to the current value. After the first change, the base has changed.
concepts.visual:
100 → increase 20% → 120
120 → decrease 20% → 96
concepts.rule: New value = Original × (1 ± p/100)

examples.question: A price increases 10% and then 10% again.

concepts.shortcut: For two changes use a+b+ab/100, with decreases treated as negative.
concepts.mistakes: +20% and −20% do NOT cancel because the bases are different.

concepts.title: Understanding Ratio
concepts.simple: A ratio compares quantities. 2:3 means every 2 equal parts of the first correspond to 3 equal parts of the second.
concepts.visual:
A : B = 2 : 3
Total parts = 5
concepts.rule: Share = Total × ratio part / sum of parts
concepts.shortcut: Find the sum of ratio parts before splitting a total.
concepts.mistakes: Never add ratio numbers to the actual quantities without finding one part.

concepts.title: Direct and Inverse Proportion
concepts.simple: Direct quantities move together; inverse quantities move in opposite directions.
concepts.visual:
More workers → fewer days
Workers × Days = constant
concepts.rule: Direct: x/y constant. Inverse: x×y constant.

examples.question: At fixed price, 2 items cost ₹100. 4 items cost?

concepts.shortcut: Ask: do both quantities move in the same direction or opposite?
concepts.mistakes: Do not use direct proportion for workers and days; they are usually inverse.

concepts.title: Average from Zero
concepts.simple: Average is the value each item would have if the total were shared equally.
concepts.visual: Values → ADD ALL → DIVIDE BY COUNT
concepts.rule: Average = Sum ÷ Number of values
concepts.shortcut: For consecutive numbers, average is often the middle number.
concepts.mistakes: Do not divide before adding every value.

concepts.title: Replacement and Combined Average
concepts.simple: A replacement changes the total first; the average changes according to total change divided by number of members.
concepts.visual: Old total → remove old → add new → divide
concepts.rule: Change in average = Change in total ÷ count

examples.question: In a group of 10, 40 is replaced by 70.
Average of 20 boys is 60; 30 girls is 70.
Average of 10 numbers is 50. Replace 30 with 80.

concepts.shortcut: Use total = average × count whenever groups combine.
concepts.mistakes: Do not average two averages directly unless group sizes are equal.

concepts.title: Cost Price and Selling Price
concepts.simple: Cost Price is what the seller paid. Selling Price is what the buyer pays.
concepts.visual:
CP → compare → SP
SP>CP = Profit
concepts.rule: Profit=SP−CP; Loss=CP−SP
concepts.shortcut: Profit% and loss% are normally calculated on CP.
concepts.mistakes: Do not calculate profit percentage on SP unless the question explicitly asks.

concepts.title: Discount and Marked Price
concepts.simple: Discount is calculated from Marked Price. Discount and profit are different ideas.
concepts.visual: MP → subtract discount → SP
concepts.rule: Discount = MP−SP
concepts.shortcut: Two discounts are not simply added.
concepts.mistakes: Always apply the second discount to the reduced price.

concepts.title: BODMAS / Order of Operations
concepts.simple: Solve brackets first, then powers, division/multiplication left to right, then addition/subtraction left to right.
concepts.visual: B → O → D/M → A/S
concepts.rule: Follow operation priority and left-to-right for equal priority.
concepts.shortcut: Do not invent a separate priority between division and multiplication; solve left to right.
concepts.mistakes: A common mistake is doing addition before multiplication.

concepts.title: Finding the Pattern
concepts.simple: Look for differences, second differences, multiplication/division, squares, cubes, primes, or alternating patterns.
concepts.visual: Write differences → check pattern → test next term
concepts.rule: Start with first differences.
concepts.shortcut: Check at least two transitions before deciding the pattern.
concepts.mistakes: Do not stop after seeing one accidental pattern.

concepts.title: Simple Interest
concepts.simple: Interest is calculated only on the original principal throughout the period.
concepts.visual: Principal → same yearly interest → add
concepts.rule: SI = P×R×T/100
concepts.shortcut: At 10%, one year interest is simply P/10.
concepts.mistakes: Do not compound the principal in simple interest.

concepts.title: Compound Interest
concepts.simple: Each period's interest is added to the amount, so the next period earns interest on interest.
concepts.rule: Amount = P(1+R/100)^n

examples.question: Difference between CI and SI for 2 years at 10% on 1000

concepts.shortcut: For 2 years, CI−SI = P(R/100)^2.
concepts.mistakes: Do not calculate every year separately if the multiplier is easy.

concepts.title: Core Idea
concepts.simple: Time & Work questions become easier when information is converted into a table, equation, or diagram before calculation.
concepts.visual: Read data → organize → choose formula → calculate → verify
concepts.rule: Use the simplest valid method.
concepts.shortcut: Write units and conditions before calculating.
concepts.mistakes: Do not use a shortcut before understanding the base method.

concepts.title: Compass and Turns
concepts.simple: Always draw a tiny compass. This prevents confusion in long questions.
concepts.visual:
N
W ←  +  → E
      S
concepts.rule: Right/left depends on current facing direction.

examples.question: Face North; right, right, left, then U-turn.

concepts.shortcut: Physically rotate your finger or draw arrows for complex turns.
concepts.mistakes: Do not use page-left/page-right after the person has turned.

concepts.title: Distance and Final Position
concepts.simple: Record each movement on a coordinate-like sketch and cancel opposite movements.
concepts.visual:
North + South → net vertical
East + West → net horizontal
concepts.rule: Net movement determines final direction.
concepts.shortcut: Cancel opposite movements before deciding direction.
concepts.mistakes: Do not add all distances together when only direction is asked.

concepts.title: Draw a Family Tree
concepts.simple: Translate every sentence into a diagram. Avoid solving entirely in your head.
concepts.visual:
Grandparent
   ↓
Parent → sibling
   ↓
Child
concepts.rule: Identify generation first, then gender.

examples.question: P is Q's father; Q is R's sister.
A is B's sister; B is C's father; C is D's brother.
steps: B parent of C and D

concepts.shortcut: Mark M/F only when given or required.
concepts.mistakes: Do not assume gender for words like sibling or cousin.

concepts.title: All / Some / No as Circles
concepts.simple: Imagine categories as circles. Only accept relationships that must be true.
concepts.visual:
All A are B: A inside B
No A is B: separate
Some: overlap exists
concepts.rule: Follow only the given logical relation.

examples.question: All cats are animals. All animals are living.
Some pens are books. All books are useful.
No A is B. Some B are C.

concepts.shortcut: Use a diagram for each statement before checking conclusions.
concepts.mistakes: 'Some A are B' does not mean all A are B.

concepts.title: Comparison Chain
concepts.simple: Turn symbols into one chain and connect only when the direction is logically valid.
concepts.visual: A > B > C → A > C
concepts.rule: Combine direct chains.
concepts.shortcut: Write a chain instead of mentally juggling symbols.
concepts.mistakes: Do not reverse a symbol accidentally when rearranging.

concepts.title: Find the Transformation
concepts.simple: Compare input and output letter by letter. Check position shift, reversal, alphabet positions, or word patterns.
concepts.visual: INPUT → observe each change → verify with another pair
concepts.rule: A=1 … Z=26 can help.
concepts.shortcut: Verify the rule using every available example.
concepts.mistakes: Do not select a rule that works for only one letter.

concepts.title: Position Counting
concepts.simple: Convert left/right or top/bottom positions into total positions carefully.
concepts.visual: Total = left rank + right rank − 1
concepts.rule: The person is counted from both sides.

examples.question: A is 5th from left and 8th from right.
A is 12th from top and 19th from bottom.

concepts.shortcut: Subtract 1 because the same person is counted twice.
concepts.mistakes: Do not simply add ranks.

concepts.title: Core Method
concepts.simple: Alphabet Test is best solved by converting clues into a structured table or diagram instead of keeping everything in memory.
concepts.visual: Clue 1 + Clue 2 → diagram/table → elimination → answer
concepts.rule: Use fixed information first, then conditional clues.
concepts.shortcut: Start with the strongest clue.
concepts.mistakes: Do not assume a position unless the clue forces it.

concepts.title: Simple Present
concepts.simple: Use for habits, routines, facts and schedules.
concepts.visual: Habit/fact → simple present
concepts.rule: He/She/It generally takes verb+s/es.
concepts.shortcut: Look for time clues such as every day, usually, always.
concepts.mistakes: Do not add -s after I/you/we/they.

concepts.title: Continuous Tenses
concepts.simple: Use continuous forms for actions in progress.
concepts.visual: Subject + be verb + verb-ing
concepts.rule: Present: am/is/are; Past: was/were.

examples.question: I ___ for two hours when he called.

concepts.shortcut: Look for now, at this moment, while.
concepts.mistakes: Do not use simple verb after is/are/was/were in continuous tense.

concepts.title: Find the Real Subject
concepts.simple: The verb agrees with the grammatical subject, not the nearest noun.
concepts.visual: Subject → ignore extra 'of...' phrase → choose verb
concepts.rule: Singular subject takes singular verb.

examples.question: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready.

concepts.shortcut: Cross out prepositional phrases temporarily to see the true subject.
concepts.mistakes: Do not match the verb with a nearby plural noun inside 'of'.

concepts.title: A, An and The
concepts.simple: Choose a/an by sound, not spelling. Use the for a specific or already identified noun.
concepts.visual:
vowel SOUND → an
consonant SOUND → a
concepts.rule: Sound matters more than first letter.

examples.question: I saw a dog. ___ dog was friendly.

concepts.shortcut: Say the word aloud if unsure.
concepts.mistakes: Do not automatically use 'an' before every word beginning with a vowel letter.

concepts.title: Recognise the Job of Each Word
concepts.simple: Ask what the word is doing: naming, replacing, describing, showing action, or linking.
concepts.visual:
Noun=name
Pronoun=replaces
Verb=action/state
Adjective=describes noun
concepts.rule: Meaning and position together identify the part of speech.

examples.question: She quickly completed the difficult task.

concepts.shortcut: Ask 'what does this word describe or modify?'
concepts.mistakes: One word can play different roles in different sentences.

concepts.title: Relationship Words
concepts.simple: Prepositions show relationships of place, time, direction or connection.
concepts.visual: in / on / at → context matters
concepts.rule: Time: at clock, on day/date, in month/year.
concepts.shortcut: Build small groups: at 5, on Monday, in June.
concepts.mistakes: Do not translate directly from Tamil; English usage must be learned as patterns.

concepts.title: Pronoun Reference
concepts.simple: A pronoun replaces a noun and must agree in number/person with its reference.
concepts.visual: Noun → matching pronoun
concepts.rule: Check who/what the pronoun refers to.
concepts.shortcut: Find the antecedent before choosing the pronoun.
concepts.mistakes: Do not let a nearby noun confuse the reference.

concepts.title: Core Skill
concepts.simple: Conjunctions requires understanding the sentence before selecting an answer. Grammar rules support meaning; they do not replace reading.
concepts.visual: Read full sentence → identify clue → apply rule → reread
concepts.rule: Meaning + grammar together give the answer.
concepts.shortcut: Read the entire sentence before choosing.
concepts.mistakes: Do not select an option only because it sounds familiar.
